The whirly tube is an aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs classification number 412.22, built from a corrugated plastic hose open at both ends, one of which may be wider. The player holds one end and swings the narrower end in a circle, and the airflow over the corrugations produces discrete notes; the faster the swing, the higher the pitch, and the pitches belong roughly to the harmonic series, like a valveless brass instrument. For concert use the tube must be trimmed to tune it. Although it is an aerophone, it is often grouped with sound-effect percussion such as chains, clappers and thunder sheets. In the late 1960s it was sold by street vendors in New York, and later appeared in theatre productions, pop and experimental music and drum and bugle corps.
旋轉管曾作為街頭玩具販售，並進入劇場製作、流行音樂與當代古典編制。它在彼得·布魯: The whirly tube has been sold as a street toy and has entered theatre productions, popular music and contemporary classical line-ups. It is used in Peter Brook's production of A Midsummer Night's Dream; a number of creators have used it, among them Peter Schickele, Frank Ticheli, Paul Simon and Macy Gray. Donald Sosin's 137 Facets is performed with flute, vibraphone and fifteen tuned whirly tubes; Brett Dean's Bliss and the Cadets drum and bugle corps have also used it.
旋轉管的主體為波紋或肋紋塑膠管／軟管，屬中空可撓圓柱，兩端開口，一端可能較寬形成: The body of the whirly tube is a corrugated or ribbed plastic tube or hose, a hollow flexible cylinder open at both ends, one of which may be wider to form a bell. It can be several feet long and a few inches wide. The blown corrugahorn needs a smaller diameter: one inch is too big and half an inch will do; Hopkin recommends 3/8 inch gas-heater hose, whose material the source does not state. Another variant, the cugaphone, does not use a corrugated tube: a trumpet mouthpiece is fitted to 3/8 inch internal-diameter plastic pipe, with a kitchen funnel as the bell at the other end; the materials of the remaining parts are not stated.
旋轉管起源不明，1960年代至1970年代以玩具形式出現，1960年代末在紐約市: The origin of the whirly tube is unknown; it appeared as a toy in the 1960s and 1970s and was briefly popular in New York in the late 1960s under a trade name, sold by street vendors. In 1973 Crawford quoted others saying that such toys had been seen in toy shops about a year or two earlier, and studied its acoustics; he also developed blown and water-piston versions. From the 1970s it came into theatre and concert use, with the tube trimmed to tune it; in 1972 a popular account discussed another variant made from a mouthpiece and a funnel, and by 1997 there was already an ensemble using it.
旋轉管音色接近純音，傅立葉分析顯示幾乎全為基音，聽感清楚而單音。發音為離散音高，: The whirly tube's timbre is close to a pure tone: Fourier analysis shows it is almost entirely fundamental, and it is heard as clear and single. It sounds discrete pitches that belong roughly to the harmonic series; one tube swung can give three or four notes, reaching the second to seventh harmonics, the seventh with effort, and commercial versions are often said to give five. Pitch and volume change with the speed of swing, the length and diameter of the tube and the spacing of the ribs; with too little air speed it does not sound, and the fundamental and low harmonics are often hard to excite. It is an aerophone, but it is often grouped with struck sound effects; compared with a tube without ribs its overtones are lower.
演奏者一手握住管身固定端，將較細的一端在空中畫圈旋轉；較長的管可握在中間，或把一: The player holds the fixed end of the tube in one hand and swings the narrower end in a circle in the air; a longer tube can be held in the middle, or one end put out of a car window. The swing makes a speed difference between the moving end and the fixed end, creating a pressure difference: air is drawn in at the fixed end and passes through the corrugations, producing vortices and pitch. The faster the swing, the higher the pitch; below a threshold air speed it does not sound. A beginner should start on harmonics two to six, which are easier to excite; the fundamental and second harmonic are harder to produce. To skip a neighbouring harmonic you must speed up suddenly; with a corrugahorn you can interrupt the airflow with the tongue and throat. For ensemble use, trim the tube to tune it first.
